research_question: What is the effect of Cerebrolysin or Cortexin (cerebral peptide mixtures), compared with placebo, on all-cause death in adults with acute ischaemic stroke?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality: number of participants who died from any cause out of the number randomised to each arm (intention-to-treat denominator), measured over the longest reported follow-up period in the trial (typically 10 to 90 days).
positive_direction: Lower mortality / fewer deaths in the Cerebrolysin or Cortexin group compared with the placebo group
search_queries: Cerebrolysin Cortexin acute ischaemic stroke randomized trial mortality
Cerebrolysin acute ischemic stroke placebo controlled trial outcome
Cortexin ischemic stroke trial death mortality quantitative
inclusion_criteria: Randomised placebo-controlled trials comparing Cerebrolysin or Cortexin (with or without concurrent standard therapy such as thrombolysis) against placebo in adults with acute ischaemic stroke
Studies reporting all-cause mortality over follow-up (using intention-to-treat randomised denominators)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, study abstracts that only summarise other trials, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between a Cerebrolysin or Cortexin arm and a placebo control arm (e.g., non-placebo or uncontrolled designs)
No extractable quantitative outcome data on all-cause mortality (deaths and randomised sample sizes) that can produce an effect size
Completely unrelated patient populations or diagnoses (e.g., haemorrhagic stroke, traumatic brain injury, dementia, or non-human animal studies)
moderators_to_extract: Concurrent acute treatment (e.g., thrombolysis vs standard medical care)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) calculated using intention-to-treat denominators (number randomised). For multi-arm trials with multiple doses against a shared placebo group, active arms are combined and compared to the single placebo group. RR < 1 indicates reduced risk of death with treatment.
